subject: Re: Redwood private deployment — SOC 2 / VPC / deployment diagram follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Chen <lauren.chen@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: private deployment / SOC 2 / VPC options (next steps)

Hi Lauren — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary from discovery:
- Acme handles customer data that includes at least some regulated records (you mentioned PHI in a subset of workflows) — HIPAA is applicable.
- Primary requirement: network isolation (VPC + private endpoints) and strong key controls; air-gapped/on-prem is a hard requirement for a subset of workloads.
- You’d like Redwood’s SOC 2 attestation and to start the vendor security questionnaire (VSQ).

What I’m going to do:
- Attach our SOC 2 Type II report and a private deployment diagram (initial) for VPC and on-prem options.
- Start the VSQ process internally and loop in Marissa (she’ll own the questionnaire responses).
- Confirm KMS/keys options and limitations for air-gapped mode.

What I need from you:
- The completed vendor questionnaire (I can accept partial answers) — I’ll attach our copy below for convenience.
- A network diagram or outline of the planned connectivity for the workloads you want isolated (public vs. private endpoints, VPN/Direct Connect, expected egress destinations).
- Any compliance timelines (audit dates / contract deadlines).

Proposed next step: a 30-min follow-up to review the network diagram and KMS options — is Friday 2026-08-07 10:00 AM PT ok?

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx (blank copy for you), redwood_soc2_report_2025.pdf (SOC 2 Type II), redwood_private_deploy_diagram.vsdx (initial topology)

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa in on the VSQ.
— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Lauren Chen <lauren.chen@acmeanalytics.com>

Cc: Daniel Ruiz <druiz@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: private deployment / SOC 2 / VPC options (next steps)

Thanks Marcus — that was helpful. A few quick notes:
- I attached our partially completed VSQ (vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx) — it's not complete but should cover most of the basics.
- We do process PHI for a subset of customers, so HIPAA/BAA is required.
- For production: either a private VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS or a fully air-gapped on-prem option is acceptable. The on-prem option will need to support nightly model updates via physically-managed media (we understand this is more manual).
- Data residency: US only for the initial rollout.

Can you confirm: does Redwood provide a BAA? And for the KMS option, can you confirm support for customer-managed keys (we prefer BYOK via AWS KMS or a Vault HSM-backed flow)?

Friday 8/7 10am PT should work for a quick call to review diagrams and KMS details — please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Chen
Head of Security & Compliance, Acme Analytics
lauren.chen@acmeanalytics.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Chen <lauren.chen@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: private deployment / SOC 2 / VPC options (next steps)

Hi Lauren — great, thanks for the quick reply and the partial VSQ. Answers inline and next steps below.

1) BAA / HIPAA
- Yes, Redwood supports a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). We have customers in healthcare and have a template BAA we can share.

2) SOC2 / GDPR
- Attached: redwood_soc2_report_2025.pdf (SOC 2 Type II). We also have a DPA for GDPR; for US-only residency we can scope that in the contract.

3) KMS / BYOK
- We support BYOK for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API we provide envelope encryption, but for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own AWS KMS key or integrate an HSM (PKCS#11) for on-prem. Key ownership and rotation policies are customer-controlled in the private deployment.

4) VPC vs Air-gapped on-prem
- VPC Private Deployment: private subnets, VPC endpoints, no public ingress to model servers. Private control plane options for Private deployments (customer VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink) depending on customer preference. Full telemetry is available via a secure metrics endpoint; we can restrict that to a collector inside your network.
- Air-gapped / On-prem: supported for a closed cluster install. Limitations: automated cloud-based model updates are unavailable (we provide an offline update process), and certain observability features will be reduced. We can provide a validated deployment bundle and a runbook for offline updates.

5) Next steps and owners
- Marissa (cc'd) will own finishing the VSQ and can intake your answers. Marissa, can you confirm your ETA for turning around the questionnaire and whether you'd like a shared Drive or Doc review?
- Dylan (cc'd) can run the deeper architecture review on the network diagram during the Friday call.

I’ve attached an initial private deployment diagram (redwood_private_deploy_diagram.vsdx) and included links to the mutual action plan in our HubSpot record. I’ll send a calendar invite for Fri 2026-08-07 10:00 AM PT.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_report_2025.pdf, redwood_private_deploy_diagram.vsdx
— Marcus

Subject: Re: Follow-up: private deployment / SOC 2 / VPC options (next steps)

Thanks Marissa — Drive works for us. A few answers / clarifications inline:
- BAA: we prefer it executed in parallel with the SOW (we can accept it as a separate legal agreement but executed before production onboarding).
- KMS: we will plan for AWS KMS BYOK for the VPC deployment. For the air-gapped on-prem workloads, we expect key custody to remain with Acme (we'll handle the HSM locally).
- Network diagram: attaching acme_network_overview.pdf — primary path is on-prem -> AWS Transit Gateway -> private VPC with no public ingress. We will provide a more detailed subnet map before the call.

I confirmed Friday 8/7 10am PT for the architecture review — please send the calendar invite. We’ll have our infra lead (Daniel) on the call.

Attachments: acme_network_overview.pdf

Best,
Lauren
